title: Testimony from a High-Quality Pig
paragraphs: “Well… I guess it’s up to us to calm the source of the waves now.”
Father mutters this in a listless tone as he stares at the crack in the waves.
“I wonder. I can tell something very serious is happening, but I can’t quite figure out what to do.”
“Oh dear… you’re right. I wonder what we should do?”
“We just need to calm the waves immediately.”
“The first thing we need to do is—”

Just as he says that, the Lazy Pig raises its hand and oinks. Lazy Pig, what on earth have you been doing all this time! If you’re no help, I’ll use Magic to turn you into roast pork… or something like that? In that hand, he’s holding something that looks like a vision crystal.
“Oink…”
“Hm? What’s wrong?”
“Oink-oink-oink, oink-oink-oink.”
“Hmm. You’re certainly right.”
“Oink-oink-oink, oink-oink… oink-oink.”
Hey, Lazy Pig. What are you saying to Father? Soon, Father nodded, furrowing his brow in displeasure at Lazy Pig’s words.
“That’s true. There’s no doubt we should take action sooner rather than later. But… if we do that, it’ll deviate significantly from what Motoyasu told me.”
“Bubub.”
“…I suppose so. Well then, we’ll have to act quickly once the wave is over.”

Ugh… I can’t get a word in edgewise because of this Lazy Pig. I turn my face toward the Older Sister. Then, it seems the kind Older Sister is about to answer me. Just as you’d expect from Father’s partner and Filo-chan’s Older Sister! I have nothing but words of gratitude!

“Elena said that while it was good we defeated Takt, the one who killed the Hero, if things continue like this, the forces that survived in the rear will catch on to the situation, and there’s no telling what kind of revenge they’ll take on us. And Lord Naofumi nodded in agreement.”
I see. That’s quite thoughtful for a Lazy Pig. It’s true—Takt’s remnants are bound to cause trouble. That’s why we should have eliminated them without letting any escape.
“But I’ve already slaughtered all his henchmen, haven’t I?”
“That’s fine if that’s all there is, but there are surely others out there.”
Oh, Father is scolding me while talking to the Lazy Pig. That’s true… Judging by the previous loop, they’re definitely out there.

“He told us, while showing us the video crystal, that we should take action sooner rather than later. Since the evidence has already been recorded, all that’s left is to show this edited footage to the King of Faubrey—Takt’s homeland and the world’s greatest superpower—and wipe out the members of the Takt faction. That’s when Lord Naofumi agreed, but expressed concern that things might turn out differently from the future described by the Spear Hero.”

Hmm… That Lazy Pig’s underhanded maneuvering is nothing short of divine. When, exactly, did he manage to film that with the video crystal? It’s truly a mystery. Well, if he’s going to serve faithfully under Father, I suppose I can let it slide.
“Finally, Elena replied with a sigh, ‘Isn’t it a bit late for that now?’ regarding the story of the future she’d heard from the Spear Hero.”

What’s that supposed to mean? Are you saying I’m wrong? For a lazy pig who’s always lying around, you sure have the nerve to say something like that. Just as I was glaring at the Lazy Pig, Father interrupted.

“So, once the wave is over, we’re heading to a place called Faubrey. Too many things have happened, so if we don’t handle this carefully, we could end up wanted all over the world. Before they start fabricating stories about us—true or false—let’s take the initiative and eliminate the negative legacy Takt left behind.”
“Understood!”
“But… if Ren and Itsuki have been killed, I wonder what will happen with the next Wave…”
At that moment, Father looked at the Seven-Star Weapons, swords, and bows floating around us.
“What should we do about these?”
Well, things will work out as they’re meant to. I’m sure Ren and Itsuki have found closure and are smiling down on us from heaven. Well then, shall we be on our way?
“Servant Weapons. In response to this dire situation, take residence within your new master and become her power!”
No sooner had I said that than the Seven-Star Weapons and the other weapons soared high into the sky and scattered.
“Eek!”
“Wh-what?! Nooo!”

At that moment, a hammer and a claw—both familiar to the Older Sister and Filo-chan—took residence within them. As expected, that claw really suits Filo-chan. The remaining two—a whip and what appeared to be a throwing weapon—floated around in the sky for a while, seemingly unable to find a handle, but eventually flew off.
“Boo.”

“Hmm… I’d heard about the Seven-Star Weapons from Motoyasu. Raphtalia, Filo, the battles ahead are bound to get even tougher. Since it seems you two have been chosen, I expect you to learn how to wield these properly.”
“Y-yes… but I’ve never used a hammer before…”
“Don’t worry, Older Sister knows how to use it, so she’ll teach you.”
Wow, just as I expected from Older Sister. She’s a pro when it comes to combat skills.
“Master, if I master this claw, will I be able to escape from the guy with the spear?”
“…Since they’re weapons of the same type, I suppose it’s not impossible.”
“Then I’ll do my best, Filo!”
“I’m rooting for you!”
“Boo!”
Filo-chan actually responded to my encouragement! That really boosts my motivation.
“Alright, let’s calm this wave down. Raphtalia, Filo—this is your first battle as heroes.”
“Um, I’m even more out of the loop than usual.”
“I’m in the same boat, so don’t worry about it.”

With that, we were able to quickly finish off the second wave. It was a scale that I could have handled on my own to begin with. Well, since we didn’t take our time fighting the wave, I didn’t get a look at the enemy that appears after the Soul Eater.
“Then let’s move on as soon as possible.”

“Before that… I’m pretty sure there’s an old woman in a nearby village who’s an incredible martial artist and served as a mentor to Father and the others. She’s supposed to be suffering from an illness, so you should use this.”

I handed the Yggdrasil potion from my spear to Father and, cross-referencing it with my knowledge from past loops, guided him toward the old woman’s house. It seems the village was spared just before the wave struck, thanks to the preventive actions of Keel and the others, as well as Lady Filolial.

Father visited the village, looking worried and asking if there were any victims of the wave. He found the old woman bedridden and prescribed her the medicine. Although the timing was slightly off, it seems she managed to survive. The old woman’s son expressed his gratitude to Father.
Father, however, is looking at me with a slightly displeased expression. After finishing his conversation, he came over to me and pointed at the old woman’s house.
“If it was just a matter of giving her medicine, couldn’t Motoyasu have done it?”
“Well, it also serves to subtly convey to the villagers that you are the true identity of the Divine Bird’s Saint, Father.”
“Damn… It’s just unpleasant being put in the spotlight by Motoyasu.”
“I understand how you feel, but all things considered, he did a lot for us over the past month and a half, so let’s just forgive him.”
“It’s not like I’m holding a grudge or anything… but it’s just really unpleasant.”

By the way, Filo-chan seems completely absorbed in mastering how to use her claws. Even after the annihilation, she was still slashing at the air with her claws. It’ll add some color to our lives from now on.
“…Boo.”
“I know. Alright, the early bird catches the worm. There was minimal damage, and we were able to end the wave immediately. Once we all head back, the representative will set out right away.”
“Roger that!”
And so, after finishing our second wave and dropping everyone off at Zeltoble, we headed for Faubrey.

Upon arriving in Faubrey, we headed straight for the castle. Well, it seemed the people in Faubrey were quite perplexed by the current situation as well. After all, several of the church lights—which serve as proof that the Heroes have been summoned and are active—had suddenly gone out. Moreover, if two of the Four Holy Heroes and four of the Seven Star Heroes were to vanish all at once, that would truly be a huge commotion. Well, since two of the Seven Star Heroes’ lights relit, the scale of the confusion seemed to be somewhat less severe.

Amidst all that, it was us who made a sudden triumphant return. We appeared via a portal in front of the castle; I brandished my spear while Father held up his shield as we made contact with the gatekeeper. We then proceeded straight to the reception desk and successfully secured an audience with the Pig King.
“King Faubrey has arrived. The Spear Hero and the Shield Hero—though this is an unexpected visit, the King is said to welcome you both.”
“So, what brings you here today? I’ve heard the King is very interested in the heroes’ business.”
I’d told Father-in-law beforehand what kind of person the Pig King was, so he remained calm. On the other hand, Big Sister and Filo-chan both furrowed their brows when they saw the Pig King.
“Ah, this guy’s handy for explaining that matter, so please listen to him.”
“Bubububu, oink.”
“Buhuhuhu, hmm…”
“It shouldn’t be a bad deal for you, right? It’s free just to listen, after all.”

After introducing himself as if he were Father’s assistant—or rather, as a “Lazy Pig”—he activated what appeared to be an edited video crystal. It showed the moment Takt raised his sword and unleashed Skills while spouting cocky lines, as well as his subsequent selfish behavior. What’s more, he’s included footage of the Pope of the Three Heroes Church and his abusive remarks as well. Honestly… I just can’t figure out when on earth Lazy Pig managed to film all this.

The members of Faubrey, who had been on high alert ever since Takt—the Whip Hero—disappeared, along with Ren and Itsuki at the same time, were viewing the footage presented by the Lazy Pig with a look of skepticism.
“Your Majesty! You must not lend an ear to such nonsense. One might even wonder if they are the true Heroes…”

It was a group of ministers—presumably from the Takt faction—who butted in at that point. They were desperately pointing at us, shouting things like, “These are the ones who killed the hero!” and making all sorts of baseless accusations, but the Pig King is quite sensitive to such matters.
“Buhahaha… Well then, wouldn’t it be best to hear from Takt himself, the one under suspicion? You say the Four Holy Heroes are telling lies? Well, that is, if Takt is actually still alive.”

Just as he had when we all went to Faubrey in the previous loop, the Pig King—judging that he could discreetly deal with Takt’s remnants—came to our defense. Shortly after that, an audit of Takt was launched under the pretext of a follow-up investigation. The investigation revealed that Takt’s inner workings were completely corrupt. The testimonies from Zeltoble’s Dark Guild and the Merchants’ Guild also served to back this up.

Apparently, it came to light that Takt was the culprit behind a gruesome murder of a merchant that occurred when Father was promoted to an executive position. Apparently, they had made a deal to rise through the ranks anonymously in Zeltoble’s Colosseum, enter into a contract with the merchant they’d killed, and have the slave transferred to them. However, since I thwarted that scheme and things didn’t go as planned, they selfishly stormed the merchant’s place, killed him, and seized the slave.

According to Father and the merchant in Zeltoble, if he wanted them that badly, he should have just bought them with money… That’s exactly right. Given Takt’s wealth, buying a single slave would have been a piece of cake.

Apparently, Takt is actually quite stingy. What’s more, he apparently avoided using his authority as a hero to forcibly seize them because it would draw too much attention… Did he really think murdering a merchant wouldn’t attract attention? I also can’t fathom why he’d go to the trouble of snatching a filthy pig. If it were Father, he’d simply reinvest the profits elsewhere. This, too, highlights the difference in business acumen between Takt and Father.

Incidentally, as if to corroborate the story, it seems they found the “pig”—the daughter of an indebted noble who was a target for capture—inside the airship that had been docked at Melromarc. What’s more, a “stalker pig,” one of Itsuki’s associates, was reportedly captured alive and tortured.

So it seems Takt defaulted on this “debt-ridden aristocrat pig’s” debt. According to this pig’s testimony, she had been planning to undergo plastic surgery and change her name on Takt’s estate later, along with her parents. That dream has been cruelly shattered, and now she’s back in Zeltoble. It’s entirely her own fault.

I digressed a bit there. It seems the one captured alive by Takt was the Stalker Pig. Well, the stalker pig is a high-class pig, even among pigs. He was good enough to catch my attention back in the day, so I suppose he’d caught Takt’s eye as well. Apparently, Takt captured him right after killing Itsuki and tried to win him over by brainwashing him into believing who the true hero was, but the stalker pig didn’t show the slightest sign of cooperating, so they were reportedly considering whether to dispose of him?
Either way, they’re a hopeless bunch. However, the Stalker Pig, having been rescued like this, testified as a living witness that Itsuki had been killed by Takt.

As a result, every faction that defended Takt was wiped out one by one. What’s more, before anyone knew it, all sorts of embellishments had been added to the story, and even my killing of the Crimson Swine in Melromarc ended up being blamed on Takt. It’s also said that regarding the aftermath of the revolution in the neighboring country that Itsuki was involved in, as well as the dragon zombie incident that Ren was involved in, it was made to look as though Takt had killed them both while they were rushing to the scene to re-investigate the cases. It’s a real shame to be so thoroughly exposed as a self-serving schemer. I was struck by how Father muttered, “The human heart and rumors are terrifying.”

Oh, right—it seems Takt and his group ended up defeating the dragon zombies. So, retrieving our Rival was impossible. Well, there’s no point in expecting someone who isn’t there. After all, we can save the world even without a dragon! HAHAHA

Taking advantage of all this commotion, the Queen of Melromarc returned with her Finacée and succeeded in subduing Trash. Thanks to the added embellishments in the rumors, Trash was reportedly disheartened upon hearing that the Crimson Swine had been killed by Takt. Still, it seems he had enough energy left to blame it all on Father.

According to the story, while searching for the uncontactable Crimson Swine, he interfered with the guild and was posting appeals on bulletin boards when Takt rushed over. It’s said he planned to secure permission for domestic activities, promote collaboration among heroes, and plot the assassination of Father on the day of reckoning. To that dejected Trash, the Queen—who knew Crimson Swine well—reportedly said this:
“Malty, who’d grown tired of the Spear Hero and fled, went to Takt, his boyfriend from his student days, and was taken advantage of.”
And she apparently showed the Trash some compromising evidence of Crimson Swine’s lewd behavior from his student days.

In any case, it’s all thanks to the Pope of the Three Heroes Church colluding with Takt. Well, it’s also partly because the faith was already in shambles thanks to Father. I get the feeling Takt was the one who delivered the final blow, though. As a last-ditch excuse, the Pope’s subordinates apparently claimed he was the one who did it all. They supposedly mentioned something about faith in me—the Spear Hero—or something like that? Well, that part doesn’t really matter. The number of heroines in Seven All—just a few left.
